title: Locators and their priority order
summary: Locators find elements the way users do. Prefer getByRole, then getByLabel, getByPlaceholder, getByText, getByAltText/getByTitle, then getByTestId; CSS/XPath last.
why: Tests that depend on ids, classes or DOM structure break on harmless refactors. User-facing locators only break when what the user sees changes — which is exactly when a test should fail.
body:
A Locator is a recipe, not an element: it is resolved every time you use it, so it never goes stale, and it auto-waits. Locators are strict — if one matches several elements, actions throw so you notice. Narrow down by chaining (list.getByRole('listitem')) and filtering (filter({ hasText }), filter({ has })). New in 1.64: locator.within(parent) reads as 'this, within that'.

Use getByTestId when there is no user-facing handle (a canvas, a dynamic id), and agree a data-testid convention with developers.
objectives: Know when getByTestId is the right choice
pitfalls: Using .first()/.nth() to silence strictness instead of writing a better locator.
